headline: Revenue and margins grow, tax resolution lifts EPS
summary_short: AT&T grew Q2 FY2026 revenue 2.3% y/y to $31,558M and operating income 8.3% y/y to $7,038M, with diluted EPS of $0.66 (+6.5% y/y) helped by a lower 13.5% effective tax rate after an IRS examination resolution; cash rose to $17,570M ahead of the pending ~$23B EchoStar spectrum purchase.
summary_long: Revenue rose 2.3% y/y on higher Advanced Connectivity fiber and wireless revenue, including the acquired Lumen fiber business, partly offset by declining Legacy copper revenue. Operating income rose 8.3% y/y to $7,038M as revenue growth outpaced a 2.4% rise in operations-and-support costs and a 5.4% drop in D&A. Net income was $4,627M (diluted EPS $0.66, +6.5% y/y); a lower 13.5% tax rate (vs 20.3%, on an IRS resolution) offset 13.8% higher interest expense. Cash rose to $17,570M ahead of the pending ~$23,000M EchoStar spectrum purchase. AT&T bought back $2,177M of stock and paid a $0.2775/share dividend this quarter. No forward guidance was restated in this filing.

Reflects higher operating income and a lower 13.5% effective tax rate, down from 20.3% a year ago, following the resolution of certain IRS examinations.

Revenue growth of 2.3% outpaced a 2.4% rise in operations and support costs (asset-abandonment charge, advertising, bad-debt expense, partly offset by transformation savings) and a 5.4% drop in D&A from fully depreciated legacy assets.

Higher operating income and a lower 13.5% effective tax rate were partly offset by 13.8% higher interest expense on higher debt balances/rates and a swing to a $29M equity-affiliate loss after the 2025 sale of the DIRECTV Entertainment Holdings stake.
Tracks the basic-EPS move; diluted weighted shares fell 3.8% y/y on prior buyback activity, adding per-share lift on top of the net-income increase.

Reflects share buybacks: AT&T repurchased $2,177M of stock (86 million shares) this quarter under its $10,000M repurchase authorizations.
Balance remained elevated ahead of the pending ~$23,000M EchoStar spectrum-license purchase, which AT&T expects to close by end of July 2026 using cash on hand and term-loan borrowings.
Retained earnings grew with $8,456M of six-month net income, partly offset by $3,860M of common dividends and treasury-stock repurchases; not separately explained in the release.
